records.label: Cement grout coverage as published by two manufacturers, and the joint model and powder density each table implies
records.source_name: MAPEI Ultracolor Plus FA technical data sheet (Edition Date: August 28, 2026); LATICRETE PERMACOLOR Grout data sheet DS-250-0926
records.scope: Two cement-based grouts sold in the United States, as each maker tabulates its coverage by tile size and joint width. Tables transcribed from the PDF text; Calculiva keeps an archived copy of both PDFs as read and does not republish them. The implied density is derived here from each table, it is not a figure the makers print.

model.joints: one tile length plus one tile width of joint per tile, crossings counted twice: lb per sq ft = rho × (L + W) × g × d / (L × W), inches
model.depth: the tile thickness printed in the table

model.joints: exact grid: joint area per tile = (L + g)(W + g) − L × W, over the tile plus joint
model.depth: the tile thickness printed in the table

derived.rule: For every table cell, implied density = bag weight / (sq ft covered × joint volume per sq ft). Joint volume per sq ft = 144 × (L + W) × g × d / (L × W) cu in for the simple model, 144 × ((L + g)(W + g) − L × W) / ((L + g)(W + g)) × d for the exact grid. Median over the cells; p10-p90 shown.
derived.note: Both makers land within 1 lb/cu ft of each other (about 97.5 to 98.5 lb of powder per cubic foot of joint) but on different joint models; the simple model counts each crossing twice and grows past the exact grid as joints widen on small tiles.

records.label: Nominal and actual dimensions of softwood boards sold in the United States
records.source_name: PS 20, American Softwood Lumber Standard (NIST) — table "Boards dressed, S4S, dry" as reproduced by the Southern Forest Products Association
records.scope: softwood boards surfaced four sides (S4S) and dried, sold at retail in the United States. DOES NOT APPLY to MDF, PVC or composite moldings: see trim-nominal-actual-mdf.
records.note: The current edition of the standard is PS 20-25 (effective January 2025, supersedes PS 20-20 Revision 1); its Table 3, read on 2026-10-01, gives the same inch values as the reproduced table. The reproduction rounds metric equivalents to the millimeter (1-1/2 in appears as 38 mm), PS 20-25 gives them to the tenth (38.1 mm). The engine converts from inches at full precision: 1.5 in = 38.1 mm.

records.label: Bulk soil and fill: loose and in-place weights per cubic yard, how bulk and bagged soil must be sold, and the vehicle payload label
records.source_name: NIST Handbook 130 (2026 edition), Sections IV-A and IV-B; Caterpillar, Earthwork volumes reference tables; NHTSA interpretation of FMVSS No. 110, S4.3
records.scope: Soil, topsoil and fill dirt bought for a residential project in the United States, in bags or in bulk. The weights are Caterpillar's reference values for earthmoving; the source itself says weight varies with moisture, grain size and compaction, so they are used as published figures, not as the weight of a given load. The sale rules are the NIST uniform regulations that states adopt; whether a state has adopted a given section is not checked here.

bulk.rule: Top soil, fill dirt, aggregate or chipped rock, sand (including concrete and mortar sand), decomposed granite, landscape type rock, and cinders must be sold by the cubic meter or cubic yard or by weight.
bulk.section: Handbook 130 (2026), IV-B Uniform Regulation for the Method of Sale of Commodities, 2.29. Sand, Rock, Gravel, Stone, Paving Stone

mulch.rule: All mulch shall be sold, offered, or exposed for sale in terms of volume measure in SI units in terms of the cubic meter or liter or in U.S. customary units in terms of the cubic yard or cubic foot.

dry_measure.rule: dry measure U.S. bushel of 2150.42 in3, or peck, dry quart, and dry pint subdivisions of the bushel
dry_measure.label_rule: Whenever the declaration of quantity is in terms of the dry pint or dry quart, the declaration shall include the word “dry.”
dry_measure.section: Handbook 130 (2026), IV-A Uniform Packaging and Labeling Regulation, units table and 6.7.2. Units of Two or More Meanings
dry_measure.note: One dry quart is 1/32 of the bushel, 67.200625 cubic inches; a cubic foot therefore holds 25.714 dry quarts, not 20 and not the 29.922 liquid quarts.

weights.source: Caterpillar, Earthwork volumes reference tables, Common materials loose & bank table

definitions.loose: Loose Cubic Yards (LCY): Material which has been excavated in some way and swelled as a result of the space that now exist between its elements.
definitions.bank: Bank Cubic Yards (BCY)/Bank Cubic Meters (BCM): Material as it lies in its natural bank state.
definitions.compact: Compact Cubic Yards (CCY)/Compact Cubic Meters (CCM): Material which has been compacted and become more dense as a result.
definitions.load_factor_reading: Calculiva's reading of the table: in the five rows used here, loose weight ≈ bank weight x load factor, within the rounding of the source table (1,600 ≈ 2,300 x 0.70 for top soil), so a loose cubic yard brought back to bank density occupies the load factor of a cubic yard.

weights.caveat: Weight of material varies with moisture content, grain size, degree of compaction, etc. Tests must be made to determine exact material characteristics.

payload_label.rule: S4.3(a) requires that each placard show vehicle "capacity weight" expressed as "The combined weight of occupants and cargo should never exceed XXX kilograms or XXX pounds."
payload_label.location: the vehicle placard on the driver's side B-pillar
payload_label.source: NHTSA, interpretation of FMVSS No. 110, Tire Selection and Rims, S4.3
payload_label.note: The figure covers occupants and cargo together: the driver and passengers are subtracted from it before the soil.

records.notes: CTEF specifies the side being offset above 15 nominal inches and manufacturer exceptions. One-third in the geometric model is 33.333... percent; it must not be represented as exact compliance with a 33 percent limit. The 1-inch sliver warning in the existing engine is a product planning flag, not an installation standard. records.label: Actual dimensions of primed MDF boards sold in the United States
records.source_name: The Home Depot, MDF Boards / Primed category — "Common" and "Actual" labels on the product pages
records.scope: primed MDF boards sold at retail in the United States. MDF is NOT covered by PS 20: its actual thickness differs from that of softwood.
records.note: Central finding: primed MDF is 11/16 in thick (reading: 0.669 in on one product page) where PS 20 gives 3/4 in for a softwood board of the same nominal size. The WIDTHS, however, match PS 20. Applying the softwood standard to MDF therefore gives a thickness that is wrong by 1/16 in — which matters when a batten butts against an existing baseboard.

product_calculator.inputs: Wall Width (ft), Wall Height (ft), Add Window / Door with width and height in feet; product width, length and repeat read from the product page
product_calculator.rule: strip height = height rounded up to whole repeats when the repeat is above zero, else the height, with no trim; strips = ceil(wall width / roll width) minus floor(opening width / roll width) for each opening; strips per roll = floor(roll length / strip height); rolls = ceil(strips / strips per roll); 'Roll is too short' when a strip exceeds the roll. Openings are saved in the browser's localStorage and persist across product pages until removed.
